story: We are a trucking company with 40 trucks. Every Monday our office manager spends about 6 hours copying fuel card data and route data from 3 spreadsheets into one report for the owner. By the time he reads it, it's already old.

followups.question: Do the 3 sheets use the same truck numbers?
followups.answer: No, fuel cards use card numbers, routes use plate numbers

story: Dental clinic with 3 dentists. Patient intake forms come in as PDFs and paper. Our front desk retypes them into our practice software and insurance details get missed all the time, so claims get rejected.
Small law firm, 6 lawyers. Clients keep asking the same questions about their contracts and deadlines. We search through hundreds of PDF contracts by hand to answer, it takes hours every week.

We sell handmade candles on Shopify. Every evening I copy new orders into a Google Sheet for our supplier and our accountant, about 30 minutes a day. Sometimes I make mistakes and the supplier ships the wrong scent.

We are an ISO in payment processing. Every month we calculate commission splits for 30 sales agents from 3 processor reports. Agents get 40% to 60% of residuals depending on their deal. It takes our finance person 2 full days each month and agents argue about the numbers.

followups.question: Who approves the splits before payout?

story: Plumbing company, 12 technicians. Jobs are written on paper, then my wife enters them into QuickBooks at night. We never know which jobs were profitable and invoices go out late.

Private school with 400 students. Teachers enter grades in our school app, but parents want a monthly progress summary and teachers write those by hand. It takes each teacher a full evening every month.
Real estate agency. We get leads from Zillow, our website, Facebook and phone calls. Agents copy them into a spreadsheet and fight over who got which lead. Many leads never get a call back.
We run a B2B SaaS with an AI chat assistant for our customers. Our AI bill went from $2k to $11k a month in 4 months and we don't know which features or customers cause it. Our data is in Postgres.
We make metal parts for car makers. Quality inspectors write defects in Excel at each machine, and once a week the quality manager tries to find patterns. By then we already made bad parts for days.
